subject: psychiatry
title: Other psychotic disorders

steps.tx: Clinicians separate psychotic disorders mainly by **duration of illness**, breadth of symptoms and overlap with mood episodes. **Brief psychotic disorder** starts suddenly with delusions, hallucinations or disorganised behaviour and lasts under one month. Patients return fully to their previous level of functioning after the episode resolves completely. Marked stress often precedes the episode and helps clinicians understand the presentation. Schizophreniform disorder resembles schizophrenia closely but lasts between one and six months only.
steps.say: Clinicians separate psychotic disorders mainly by duration, symptom breadth and mood overlap together. Brief psychotic disorder starts suddenly and lasts for under one month only. Patients return fully to previous functioning after the brief episode resolves completely. Schizophreniform disorder is similar to schizophrenia but lasts between one and six months.

steps.tx: Patients with **delusional disorder** sustain one or more delusions for at least one month with otherwise near normal functioning. Hallucinations remain minimal and usually relate directly to the delusional theme when they occur. Common themes include erotomanic, grandiose, jealous, persecutory and somatic beliefs that dominate thinking. **Jealous delusions** and **erotomanic delusions** carry important risks because patients may confront, stalk or attack other people. Behaviour outside the delusional system often appears rational and makes engagement more difficult.
steps.say: Patients with delusional disorder have fixed delusions for at least one month. Functioning outside the delusional belief often remains surprisingly intact during daily life. Jealous beliefs and erotomanic beliefs carry risks because patients may confront others. Clinicians assess risk carefully and engage patients without directly challenging fixed beliefs initially.

steps.tx: Patients with **schizoaffective disorder** have a major mood episode together with active psychosis for most of the illness. They also need at least two weeks of delusions or hallucinations without prominent mood symptoms. This **psychosis without mood** proves that psychosis occurs independently from the mood episode. The disorder divides into bipolar type and depressive type according to the mood episodes present. Clinicians use longitudinal timelines from collateral history because cross sectional impressions often mislead diagnosis.
steps.say: Patients with schizoaffective disorder have mood episodes together with psychosis during illness. They also have psychosis for two weeks without prominent mood symptoms present. This independent psychosis helps clinicians separate schizoaffective disorder from primary mood disorders. Clinicians use longitudinal timelines because single cross sectional assessments often mislead diagnosis considerably.

steps.tx: Clinicians must exclude **secondary psychosis** before labelling any presentation as a primary psychiatric disorder. Important causes include stimulants, cannabis, steroids, withdrawal states, delirium, dementia and temporal lobe epilepsy. **Autoimmune encephalitis** can present with psychosis, seizures and movement abnormalities in young women with ovarian teratoma. Thyroid disease and other endocrine disorders also cause psychotic symptoms in some patients. New psychosis after forty years with visual hallucinations, confusion or neurological signs demands prompt medical investigation.
steps.say: Clinicians must exclude secondary psychosis before labelling any presentation as primary psychiatric illness. Important causes include stimulant use, steroid treatment, delirium and temporal lobe epilepsy. Autoimmune encephalitis can present with psychosis and seizures in young women. New psychosis after forty years with confusion requires prompt medical investigation first.

steps.tx: This axial MRI image shows bright **FLAIR hyperintensity** in both medial temporal lobes with a normal comparison image beside it. The label links this pattern to **anti NMDA receptor encephalitis**, an important medical cause of psychosis. Students should remember that bilateral temporal signal change with psychosis should trigger a search for autoimmune disease. The image matters because **secondary psychosis** needs medical treatment rather than antipsychotic treatment alone.
steps.say: This MRI image presents bright signal change in both medial temporal lobes bilaterally. The label links this pattern to autoimmune encephalitis presenting with prominent psychosis. Students should search for medical causes when imaging shows bilateral temporal lobe abnormality. Secondary psychosis needs medical treatment and not antipsychotic treatment alone in hospital.
